우리.t: Koreans say 우리 where English says 'my': 우리 엄마 (my mom), 우리 집 (my home).

세계.x: I want to travel to many countries around the world.
세계.e: Both parts point to 'world'. 세계 지도 = world map.

시험.x: I have a Korean exam next week.
시험.t: 'Take an exam' is 시험을 보다 (literally 'see an exam').

이유.x: What's the reason you were late?
이유.e: Literally 'reason + cause' — 왜? (why?) is answered with an 이유.

출발하다.m: to depart, to leave, to set off
출발하다.x: The train departs from Seoul Station at ten.
출발하다.e: Literally 'go out and set off'; opposite: 도착하다 (arrive).

너무.forms: 너무 + adjective/verb: 너무 비싸요, 너무 좋아요
너무.e: From 넘다 (to go over) — 'too much'; now often just means 'so, really'.
너무.t: Originally negative ('too much'), but now also used positively: 너무 좋아요 = I love it.

벌써.e: 벌써 = already; 아직 = still, not yet.
벌써.t: 벌써 often shows surprise that something happened sooner than expected.

에게.x: I wrote a letter to my mother.
에게.e: Polite/written; 한테 is the casual version. 친구에게 = to a friend.
에게.t: For places or things use 에; for people and animals use 에게/한테.

주문.x: You can order over there at the counter.
주문.e: Literally 'note down in writing': writing down what the customer wants.
주문.t: Servers ask "주문하시겠어요?", which means "Are you ready to order?"

마음에 들다.forms: N이/가 마음에 들어요 · 마음에 드세요? (ㄹ drops)
마음에 들다.m: to like, to be pleased with
마음에 들다.ex: 이 가방 색깔이 정말 마음에 들어요.
마음에 들다.x: I really like the color of this bag.
마음에 들다.e: Literally 'to enter the heart' — what you like gets into your heart.
마음에 들다.t: The liked thing is the subject: 이 옷이 마음에 들어요, not 이 옷을.

비자.ex: 유학을 가려면 먼저 학생 비자를 받아야 해요.
비자.x: To study abroad, you first have to get a student visa.

늘다.forms: 늘어요 · 늘었어요 · 늘 거예요 · 는 (+noun) (ㄹ drops)
늘다.m: to increase, to grow; to improve (skills)
늘다.x: I practiced every day, so my cooking skills improved.
늘다.e: Causative 늘리다 'to increase something' comes from it.

싱겁다.x: If the soup is a little bland, add salt.
싱겁다.e: Also describes people: 싱거운 사람 tells silly, flat jokes.
싱겁다.t: 싱겁다 means not salty enough, not 'tasteless'; its opposite is 짜다 'salty'.

만남.ex: 우리의 첫 만남은 학교 앞 작은 도서관에서였어요.
만남.x: Our first meeting was at a small library in front of the school.
만남.e: From 만나다 'to meet' plus the noun ending -ㅁ.

그분.x: That person is the principal of our school.
그분.e: 그 'that' + 분 'honorable person'; the polite form of 그 사람.

나다.m: to come out, to appear; to happen, to break out; to grow
나다.x: Suddenly there was a strange sound outside.
나다.e: A super-productive verb: 화가 나다, 사고가 나다.
나다.t: Learn it in chunks: 열이 나다 (have a fever), 냄새가 나다 (smell), 생각이 나다 (come to mind).

도움이 되다.forms: N에 도움이 돼요 · 도움이 됐어요 · 도움이 될 거예요
도움이 되다.m: to be helpful, to help, to be useful
도움이 되다.ex: 이 책이 한국어 공부에 도움이 많이 됐어요.
도움이 되다.x: This book really helped with my Korean studies.
도움이 되다.t: The helpful thing is the subject and the area takes 에: 운동이 건강에 도움이 돼요.

토끼.x: The rabbit is happily eating a carrot.
토끼.e: Koreans see a rabbit pounding rice cakes on the moon.

부서.x: I work in my company's marketing department.
부서.t: To ask someone's department, say 어느 부서에서 일하세요?

대출.x: I took out a loan from the bank to buy a house.
대출.t: It also means checking out library books: 도서 대출.

엉덩이.x: I sat for so long that my bottom hurts.

가난.ex: 그는 어릴 때 가난 때문에 학교를 그만뒀어요.
가난.x: He quit school as a child because of poverty.
가난.e: Probably from an old Sino-Korean word for 'hardship'; add 하다 for 'poor': 가난하다.

제출하다.x: Please hand in your homework by Friday.
제출하다.e: Literally 'hold up and put out': you hand something in.

표시하다.m: to mark, to indicate; to express
표시하다.ex: 지도에 우리 집 위치를 표시해 주세요.
표시하다.x: Please mark where our house is on the map.
표시하다.t: It can express feelings too: 감사의 뜻을 표시하다 means to express one's thanks.

요가.x: These days I'm doing yoga every morning.

결재.x: This document needs the president's approval.
결재.e: Literally 'decide and rule on' a document.
결재.t: Don't mix it up with 결제 'payment'; they sound the same.

소심하다.ex: 저는 소심해서 처음 보는 사람에게 말을 잘 못 걸어요.
소심하다.x: I'm timid, so I have a hard time talking to people I've just met.
소심하다.e: Literally 'small heart': a heart too small to be bold.
소심하다.t: In Chinese the same word means 'be careful', but in Korean it's a mild criticism.

임원.ex: 그는 마흔 살에 회사 임원이 되었어요.
임원.x: He became a company executive at forty.
임원.t: Pronounced [이뭔] — the ㅁ carries over to the next vowel.

안건.ex: 오늘 회의의 첫 번째 안건은 예산 문제예요.
안건.x: The first item on today's agenda is the budget.
안건.e: Literally 'proposed matter' — something put on the table.

프레젠테이션.ex: 내일 손님들 앞에서 프레젠테이션을 해야 해서 긴장돼요.
프레젠테이션.x: I'm nervous because I have to give a presentation to clients tomorrow.
프레젠테이션.e: From English 'presentation'; in offices it's often shortened to PT, read 피티.

출처.ex: 기사를 쓸 때는 출처를 꼭 밝혀야 해요.
출처.x: When you write an article, you must always cite your sources.
출처.e: Literally 'the place it came out of.'
출처.t: 출처를 밝히다 'to reveal or cite the source' is the key collocation.

한류.m: Korean Wave (popularity of Korean culture abroad)
한류.ex: 한류 덕분에 한국어를 배우는 사람이 많아졌어요.
한류.x: Thanks to the Korean Wave, more people are learning Korean.
한류.t: Pronounced [할류] — ㄴ becomes ㄹ next to ㄹ.

진솔하다.x: Everyone was moved by his candid story.

아무래도.m: it seems like, I guess, after all; no matter how you look at it
아무래도.ex: 아무래도 오늘은 비가 올 것 같아요.
아무래도.x: It looks like it's going to rain today after all.
아무래도.e: Contracted from 아무러하여도 'however it may be'.
아무래도.t: Very common with ~것 같다 to soften a conclusion you've reluctantly reached.

급속히.ex: 그 소문은 인터넷을 통해 급속히 퍼졌어요.
급속히.x: The rumor spread rapidly through the internet.

준수하다.m: to observe, to comply with, to follow (rules)
준수하다.ex: 모든 운전자는 교통 법규를 준수해야 합니다.
준수하다.x: All drivers must obey traffic laws.
준수하다.t: A formal word for rules and laws; in speech, 지키다 is far more common.

준수하다.m: handsome and talented, outstanding; decent, quite good
준수하다.x: He's good-looking and has a great personality too.
준수하다.t: Don't confuse with the verb 준수하다 (遵守) 'to obey', as in 법을 준수하다.

야무지다.ex: 그 아이는 어리지만 일을 야무지게 해요.
야무지다.x: That kid is young but does things very capably.
야무지다.t: A warm compliment, often for children or young people who are smart and handle things well.

설상가상.m: to make matters worse; one misfortune after another
설상가상.x: I got lost, and to make matters worse, it started to rain.
설상가상.e: Literally 'adding frost on top of snow'.

지표.ex: 실업률은 경제 상황을 보여 주는 중요한 지표입니다.
지표.x: The unemployment rate is an important indicator of the economy.

사돈.x: We sent a gift to our child's in-laws for the holiday.
사돈.e: English has no one word for this: the two sets of parents of a married couple.
사돈.t: The idiom 사돈 남 말 하네 means 'look who's talking.'

가슴이 뛰다.m: one's heart races, to be thrilled (with joy or anticipation)
가슴이 뛰다.ex: 내일 첫 해외여행을 간다고 생각하니 가슴이 뛰어요.
가슴이 뛰다.x: Just thinking about my first trip abroad tomorrow makes my heart race.
가슴이 뛰다.e: 뛰다 'to jump, to run': the heart beats fast with excitement.
가슴이 뛰다.t: Mostly positive excitement; 가슴이 두근거리다 is similar. For sudden fear, use 가슴이 철렁하다.

과세.x: The government tightened taxation on high earners.

도덕성.x: High moral standards are required of public officials.
도덕성.e: Literally 'the quality of the way and virtue'; -성 = -ness, -ity: 가능성, 중요성.

치유하다.ex: 음악은 상처받은 마음을 치유하는 힘이 있어요.
치유하다.x: Music has the power to heal a hurting heart.
치유하다.t: 치유 is often emotional or holistic healing, while 치료 is medical treatment.

원소.ex: 산소와 수소는 가장 흔한 원소에 속합니다.
원소.x: Oxygen and hydrogen are among the most common elements.

뒤바꾸다.m: to reverse, to switch around, to turn upside down
뒤바꾸다.ex: 그 사건은 그녀의 인생을 완전히 뒤바꿔 놓았어요.
뒤바꾸다.x: That incident completely turned her life around.
뒤바꾸다.e: Prefix 뒤- adds 'totally, upside-down' to 바꾸다; compare 뒤엎다, 뒤섞다.

오락가락.m: back and forth, coming and going; on and off
오락가락.x: It rained on and off all day.
오락가락.e: From 오다 'come' + 가다 'go' with alternating -락: come-go, come-go.
오락가락.t: 정신이 오락가락하다 means 'to drift in and out of awareness'.

간담이 서늘하다.forms: 간담이 서늘해요 · 간담이 서늘했어요 · 간담이 서늘한 + noun
간담이 서늘하다.m: to have one's blood run cold; to be chilled with fear
간담이 서늘하다.ex: 차가 갑자기 앞으로 끼어들어서 간담이 서늘했어요.
간담이 서늘하다.x: A car suddenly cut in front of me, and my blood ran cold.
간담이 서늘하다.e: Literally 'one's liver and gallbladder go cold' — organs once linked to courage.
간담이 서늘하다.t: 간담을 서늘하게 하다 = to scare someone stiff.

부제.ex: 그 책의 부제가 내용을 잘 설명해 줘요.
부제.x: The book's subtitle explains its content well.

예우하다.m: to treat with respect, to honor
예우하다.x: The nation must honor its war veterans.
예우하다.t: Common in news: 전관예우, favorable treatment given to former judges or officials.

감안하다.m: to take into account, to consider
감안하다.x: We changed the departure time, taking the weather into account.

불운.x: He didn't give up despite continued bad luck.

유일무이.m: being the one and only, unique
유일무이.ex: 이건 세상에 하나밖에 없는 유일무이한 반지예요.
유일무이.x: This is a one-of-a-kind ring; there's only one in the world.
유일무이.t: Usually 유일무이한 + noun; a stronger, more emphatic 유일한.

무고.ex: 거짓으로 신고한 사람은 무고죄로 처벌받을 수 있습니다.
무고.x: A person who files a false report can be punished for false accusation.
무고.e: Literally 'slanderous report'. Homonym warning: 무고 can also mean 'innocent' (with different characters).
무고.t: Don't mix up 무고 'false accusation' with 무고한 'innocent' (무고한 시민 'innocent citizens').

평등권.ex: 평등권은 성별이나 종교에 따른 차별을 금지합니다.
평등권.x: The right to equality forbids discrimination based on gender or religion.

교파.ex: 개신교에는 장로교, 감리교 같은 여러 교파가 있어요.
교파.x: Protestantism has many denominations, such as Presbyterian and Methodist.
교파.e: Literally 'religion branch'; -파 = faction or school: 보수파, 인상파.

샤머니즘.x: The Korean gut is a representative ritual of shamanism.
샤머니즘.e: From English 'shamanism'; the Sino-Korean term for Korean shamanism is 무속.

무신.x: In 1170, military officials staged a coup and seized power.

청동기.m: bronze ware, bronze tools; the Bronze Age
청동기.x: Social classes began to appear in the Bronze Age.
청동기.e: Literally 'blue-green copper tools' — bronze turns greenish as it ages.
청동기.t: Used alone it often means the Bronze Age, but 청동기 시대 is the full, clearer form.

근세.m: early modern times, the early modern period
근세.x: The Joseon period is often classified as the early modern era.
근세.e: Literally 'the near age' — the period just before modern times.
근세.t: Order of eras: 고대 → 중세 → 근세 → 근대 → 현대; 근세 and 근대 are easily confused.

아찔하다.ex: 높은 다리 위에서 아래를 내려다보니 아찔했어요.
아찔하다.x: Looking down from the high bridge made me dizzy.
아찔하다.e: From the mimetic 아찔 (a sudden dizzy jolt); 어찔하다 is a variant.

제반.forms: 제반 + noun: 제반 사항 · 제반 비용
제반.m: all kinds of, various, all related (things)
제반.ex: 계약에 필요한 제반 서류를 준비해 주세요.
제반.x: Please prepare all the documents required for the contract.
제반.t: Almost always used directly before a noun: 제반 사항, 제반 비용, 제반 문제.

감탄고토.m: taking what suits you and rejecting what doesn't, self-serving fickleness
감탄고토.ex: 필요할 때만 찾아오는 그 친구는 감탄고토의 전형이에요.
감탄고토.x: That friend who only comes around when he needs something is a classic opportunist.
감탄고토.e: Literally 'swallow the sweet, spit out the bitter'.
